objective.description: M3-05c: Kernel variable-radius fillet (one edge by index, radius from a start vertex to the other end) — r2: main merged (8415f7d)
acceptance_criteria: `Kernel::fillet_variable(&self, s: &Self::Shape, edge: SubShape, start: SubShape, r_start: f64, r_end: f64) -> Result<Self::Shape, KernelError>`, documented: `start` is a vertex of `edge`; the radius is `r_start` there and `r_end` at the edge's other vertex. The doc comment states the radius law between the ends, as given by OCCT's reference documentation. Implemented for `OcctKernel`; new shim code is `noexcept`, catches C++ exceptions and rejects a result `BRepCheck_Analyzer` finds invalid. Every new `unsafe` call is in `ffi` with a SAFETY comment.

Box tests (behind `occt`) on `make_box((0,0,0),(10,20,30))` (volume 6000), on the vertical edge where the planes x = 10 and y = 20 meet, with `start` its vertex at z = 0 (2→4 vertices, counts, bbox, removed volume bounds; swapped start; equal radii; input unchanged).

Errors, each with a test and never a panic, all `InvalidInput` and checked before the backend: `r_start` or `r_end` ≤ 0 or not finite; `edge` not an `Edge` or `start` not a `Vertex`; an index out of range; a `start` vertex that is not on `edge`.
A radius OCCT can't build (`r_start` 2, `r_end` 25 on that edge) returns an `Err`, not `Ok` or a panic, and the input is still usable afterwards (volume 6000).
No new dependencies. `swx-kernel` still has no workspace dependencies.
`cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test --workspace` pass, and so do the CI `swx-kernel (occt)` job commands.
QA report (FACTORY §6b) posted on the PR.
